# S6E9 at 0.94618: What Actually Moved the Score, and What Didn’t
### A measured account of 17 experiments on Predicting Electric Vehicle Purchases

**Author:** Jeff Roberts ([@jayhawk1900](https://www.kaggle.com/jayhawk1900)) · **Final: public LB 0.94618**, OOF 0.94606

---

This notebook is a write-up, not a solution. Every number in it is reproduced live from
`train.csv` in a couple of minutes — no model training, no external inputs.

The score went 0.94139 → 0.94618 over seventeen versions. What is worth reading is not the
final pipeline but the shape of the journey: **one change was worth +0.0004, and eleven
others were worth approximately nothing.** Knowing which is which turns out to be the whole
problem, and the only way to know is a control group and a paired test.

## The path

| version | idea | OOF | public LB |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | LightGBM on raw features | — | 0.94139 |
| v3 | nested target encoding on over-produced values + LGB/CatBoost blend | 0.94528 | 0.94555 |
| v4 / v6 | target encoding on every column, 7-leaf trees, residual-lift features, seed bagging | 0.94557 | 0.94576 |
| v5, v8, v9 | XGBoost, CatBoost on new features, 5-seed MLP — **diversity hunt** | — | no gain |
| **v11** | **multi-resolution encoding keys + wide-tree regime** | **0.94598** | **0.94615** |
| v13 | finer resolutions, encoded digit keys, 4-seed bagging | 0.94606 | 0.94618 |
| v15 | empirical-Bayes auto smoothing, all-column digit keys | 0.94606 | 0.94618 |
| v16 | six-family model zoo — **diagnostic** | — | — |
| v17 | deterministic boundary rules as post-processing | +0.00001 | not submitted |

## The four things I would tell someone starting this competition

1. **The signal is not in the model. It is in the generator's mistakes.** A deterministic
   formula explains AUC 0.9377 of the 0.946 available. Everything above that comes from a few
   thousand income and commute values the generator over-produced, whose observed buy rates
   drift away from the formula.
2. **Encoding *resolution* beat every other idea by an order of magnitude.** Encoding income
   at several bin widths at once was worth +0.0004. Four new model families, between them,
   were worth +0.00001.
3. **Six model families correlate above 0.97 with each other.** When the features hand every
   learner nearly sufficient statistics, ensembling has nothing left to exploit. A plain
   logistic regression beat both a neural net and a random forest here.
4. **Most ideas fail, and you cannot tell which without a control.** Digit decomposition,
   the original dataset, exact-twin matching, boundary rules, four model classes: all
   measured, all ≈ 0.0000. Each was reported as helpful by somebody.

*Acknowledgements: the multi-resolution "smooth keys" and the deterministic flags came from
public S6E9 notebooks and discussions — credited inline at each section. The recovered
generator rule is public community work; §3 verifies it independently on `train.csv`.*

```python
# ── Setup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Only train.csv is needed. Nothing here trains a model; every figure is computed
# directly from the data so you can check the claims rather than take my word.
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams.update({'figure.figsize': (9, 4), 'axes.grid': True, 'grid.alpha': 0.25,
                     'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False, 'font.size': 10})

hits = [r for r, _, f in os.walk('/kaggle/input') if 'train.csv' in f]
hits.sort(key=lambda p: (0 if 'playground-series-s6e9' in p else 1, len(p)))
train = pd.read_csv(f'{hits[0]}/train.csv')
train['y'] = (train['Will_Buy_EV'] == 'Yes').astype(int)
FEATURES = [c for c in train.columns if c not in ('id', 'Will_Buy_EV', 'y')]

print(f'{len(train):,} rows · {len(FEATURES)} features · {train.y.mean():.2%} positive')
print(f'missing values: {int(train[FEATURES].isna().sum().sum())} · '
      f'duplicate feature rows: {int(train.duplicated(FEATURES).sum())}')
```

## 1. The data is clean, which is itself informative

No missing values, no duplicate rows. That rules out two common sources of easy gains —
duplicate-matching between train and test, and missingness patterns that leak the target.
It also says the generator ran cleanly, so any exploitable structure will be statistical
rather than mechanical.

The cell below ranks each feature by how much it separates buyers from non-buyers on its
own. The point is how concentrated the signal is.

```python
# Single-feature separation: for categoricals, the spread in buy rate across levels;
# for numerics, the same over deciles. A crude but honest measure of "does this matter".
rows = []
for c in FEATURES:
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(train[c]) and train[c].nunique() > 20:
        g = train.groupby(pd.qcut(train[c], 10, duplicates='drop'), observed=True).y.mean()
    else:
        g = train.groupby(c, observed=True).y.mean()
    rows.append({'feature': c, 'levels': train[c].nunique(), 'buy-rate spread': g.max() - g.min()})

sep = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values('buy-rate spread', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
display(sep.style.format({'buy-rate spread': '{:.3f}'}).hide(axis='index'))
```

Four features carry nearly everything: subsidy, range anxiety, environmental concern and
income. The other nine barely move the buy rate at all. Hold that thought — §3 explains
exactly why it is those four and not the others.

## 2. The generator over-produced certain income values

This is the finding the whole pipeline is built on.

A typical income value appears about 8 times in 668,665 rows. But **2,213 specific values
appear 100+ times, covering 68% of all rows.** Those are values the generator copied
repeatedly out of its source data. And the buy rate at those values does not match their
neighbours: the cell below compares each over-produced value against ordinary incomes within
±$3,000, and counts how many deviate beyond chance.

#### 🔹 Cell 0: Markdown
```markdown
# EV purchase prediction: one feature hypothesis, two models

**Fahmid Arman · Playground Series S6E9**

Can a tree model benefit from treating a repeated numerical value as both a number and a category? This notebook tests that question on the synthetic [Predicting Electric Vehicle Purchases](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s6e9) dataset, with a fixed validation design and a small CPU budget.

The workflow has three comparisons: LightGBM on the original features, the same LightGBM with three categorical copies of numerical features, and their equal probability blend. Every training row receives an out-of-fold prediction. Early stopping uses a separate split **inside** each training fold, then the model is refit before scoring the untouched outer fold.

This is an exploratory ablation, not a claim of a leading solution. Reusing folds to choose features and models introduces selection optimism. Synthetic benchmark results do not establish performance on real EV buyers or explain causes of buying.
```

#### 🔹 Cell 1: Markdown
```markdown
## Task, provenance, and how to run

Predict `P(Will_Buy_EV = Yes)` for each test `id`. The metric is ROC-AUC, with `Yes=1` and `No=0`; larger is better. AUC measures ranking, not probability calibration. The submission contains `id,Will_Buy_EV` in the template's order.

Attach the official competition data to this notebook and run all cells on CPU. `RUN_TRAINING=True` trains both five-fold models. No download, installation, account connection, or automatic upload is performed. The local reference runs took about 5.5 minutes combined on a two-thread CPU configuration; Kaggle runtime and exact floating-point results may differ. Memory and folds are kept serial.

#### 🔹 Cell 0: Markdown
```markdown
# EV purchase prediction: one feature hypothesis, two models

**Fahmid Arman · Playground Series S6E9**

Can a tree model benefit from treating a repeated numerical value as both a number and a category? This notebook tests that question on the synthetic [Predicting Electric Vehicle Purchases](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s6e9) dataset, with a fixed validation design and a small CPU budget.

The workflow has three comparisons: LightGBM on the original features, the same LightGBM with three categorical copies of numerical features, and their equal probability blend. Every training row receives an out-of-fold prediction. Early stopping uses a separate split **inside** each training fold, then the model is refit before scoring the untouched outer fold.

This is an exploratory ablation, not a claim of a leading solution. Reusing folds to choose features and models introduces selection optimism. Synthetic benchmark results do not establish performance on real EV buyers or explain causes of buying.
```

Good. So:
- Real-ish tiles (blobs) do have a few fully masked rows/cols (1 row, 5 cols) → the warning fires and 0.0 is substituted into the profile. For blobs: the substituted value 0.0 vs a typical profile mean of ~130 → a step artefact. Magnitude of the effect on A2 for blobs? Let me quantify with a corrected alternative: build the profile, then for the empty positions interpolate/drop and recompute efold on the resulting (shorter) profile — the lengths differ, so comparing raw efold-in-samples is apples-to-oranges (the reference length is n//2 = 128 samples either way). The key point: for a tile with 5 empty columns out of 256, the axis=1 profile has 5 zeros among ~130-valued entries. Does that change where the ACF crosses 1/e? Probably negligibly, but the zero entries create spurious low-frequency structure. Worth quantifying once for blobs: compute A2 with zeros substituted vs with the empty entries filled by the mean of their neighbours (i.e. no synthetic step).

Let me measure the difference so the report is evidence-based rather than hand-wavy.

cd "C:\Users\mitansh\Desktop\KAGGLE HACKATHONS\Predicting-Soil-Grain-Size-Distributions-from-Images/Model 7/Approach A" && python - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v RuntimeWarning | grep -v "ret ="
import sys, numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import spatial_features as sf
from check_spatial_features import striped, blobs, coarse_blocks
PPM = 4.552516

def acf(field, mask, axis, fill):
    f = np.where(mask, field, np.nan)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        prof = np.nanmean(f, axis=1-axis)
    prof = np.array(prof, float)
    bad = ~np.isfinite(prof)
    if bad.any():
        if fill == "zero":                       # what the frozen module does
            prof[bad] = 0.0
        else:                                    # neighbour-average reference
            idx = np.arange(len(prof))
            prof[bad] = np.interp(idx[bad], idx[~bad], prof[~bad])
    prof = prof - prof.mean()
    n = len(prof)
    return np.array([float(np.dot(prof[:n-k], prof[k:])/(np.dot(prof,prof)+sf.EPS))
                     if k < n else 0.0 for k in range(n//2)])

for name, a in (("blobs", blobs()), ("stripe_x", striped()), ("coarse16", coarse_blocks())):
    g, m, e = sf.mask_and_field(a, PPM)
    for fill in ("zero", "interp"):
        a2 = float(np.log((sf._efold(acf(e, m, 1, fill))+sf.EPS)
                          / (sf._efold(acf(e, m, 0, fill))+sf.EPS)))
        print("%-9s fill=%-6s A2=%9.6f" % (name, fill, a2))
    z = float(np.log((sf._efold(acf(e,m,1,"zero"))+sf.EPS)/(sf._efold(acf(e,m,0,"zero"))+sf.EPS)))
    i = float(np.log((sf._efold(acf(e,m,1,"interp"))+sf.EPS)/(sf._efold(acf(e,m,0,"interp"))+sf.EPS)))
    print("          |delta A2| = %.6f (frozen value %.6f)" % (abs(z-i), sf.tile_spatial(a,PPM)["A2"]))

Options:
(a) Pin absolute values: e.g. record the measured A2 for the four canonical synthetic tiles with a tolerance (a golden-value pin). The repo convention (verify.py) does exactly this: golden_checks.json pins measured reference values. A golden-value pin in the contract test would catch any silent change to the statistic, including this one. Risk: it hard-codes numbers that legitimately depend on numpy version. But for a frozen pre-registration, pinning golden values is defensible and it's how this repo already works ("written once into golden_checks.json and asserted on every subsequent run").

However: instruction 3 says the definitions are frozen; a golden pin doesn't change definitions, it just records them. And it strengthens the contract. But is it my call? The owner asked for a contract test of "behaviour, invariances, placebo sanity, determinism" (file table). A golden value pin adds fragility: if the notebook later runs on Kaggle with a different numpy, the test fails spuriously. Task 9/10 may run this test on Kaggle. Hmm. Fragile golden pins in a contract test that runs in a different environment could block a later task.

Middle ground: pin the golden values with a loose relative tolerance (e.g. 2%) — enough to catch a definition change like the A2 fill swap (0.33 absolute on -0.91 = 37% relative) while robust to library noise. That's principled: I'd say "each statistic on a named synthetic tile must reproduce within 2%, because these statistics have no tolerance budget otherwise".

def fmt(values, key):
    return "; ".join("%s=%.6f" % (n, v[key]) for n, v in values.items())


# Golden reference values, measured from the frozen module on 2026-09-29 at PPM = 4.552516 and
# asserted at max(5% relative, 0.02 absolute). Same device preprocess/verify.py uses for the 12.
# The invariance and "can this statistic move" checks are blind to a change that moves all tiles
# together; this table is not. It was added after mutation testing found that replacing _acf_along's
# zero-fill of fully masked rows/columns with neighbour interpolation escapes every other check
# (it shifts A2 on blobs by 0.334, which no separation threshold sees).

}

                "coarse16": coarse_blocks}


def test_golden_values_reproduced():
    for name, maker in GOLDEN_TILES.items():
        out = sf.tile_spatial(maker(), PPM)
        for key in sf.SPATIAL:
            want, got = GOLDEN[name][key], out[key]
            tol = max(0.05 * abs(want), 0.02)
            check("%s %s within max(5%%, 0.02) of golden" % (name, key),
                  abs(got - want) <= tol, "want %.6f got %.6f tol %.6f" % (want, got, tol))

print("whose whole line is masked out. Counts and the measured effect of that rule:")
def acf(field, mask, axis, fill):
    f = np.where(mask, field, np.nan)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        prof = np.nanmean(f, axis=1 - axis)
    prof = np.array(prof, float)
    bad = ~np.isfinite(prof)
    if bad.any():
        idx = np.arange(len(prof))
        prof[bad] = 0.0 if fill == "zero" else np.interp(idx[bad], idx[~bad], prof[~bad])
    prof = prof - prof.mean()
    n = len(prof)
    return np.array([float(np.dot(prof[:n-k], prof[k:])/(np.dot(prof,prof)+sf.EPS))
                     if k < n else 0.0 for k in range(n//2)])
for n in ("blobs", "stripe_x", "noise", "coarse16"):
    g, m, e = sf.mask_and_field(tiles[n], PPM)
    er, ec = int((m.sum(axis=1) == 0).sum()), int((m.sum(axis=0) == 0).sum())
    a0 = float(np.log((sf._efold(acf(e, m, 1, "zero"))+sf.EPS)/(sf._efold(acf(e, m, 0, "zero"))+sf.EPS)))
    a1v = float(np.log((sf._efold(acf(e, m, 1, "interp"))+sf.EPS)/(sf._efold(acf(e, m, 0, "interp"))+sf.EPS)))
    print("  %-9s empty rows=%3d empty cols=%3d  A2(zero fill)=%9.6f A2(neighbour fill)=%9.6f delta=%.6f"
          % (n, er, ec, a0, a1v, abs(a0 - a1v)))
print()
a = striped(); sf.tile_spatial(a, PPM)
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(20):
    sf.tile_spatial(a, PPM)
dt = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / 20
print("cost: %.1f ms per 256x256 tile -> about %.0f s for all 1946 materialised tiles" % (dt*1000, dt*1946))

### 2.3 Mutation sanity: every statistic can move

This is the "a statistic that is numerically constant across quite different tiles is a defect"
check the brief does not ask for but the owner did. Eight synthetic tiles, one `tile_spatial` call
each, plus the internal terms so the numbers are auditable rather than just green.

```
{{PROBE}}
```

Reading of those numbers, per statistic:

- **A1** moves: -33.761250 (stripes) to 0.000000 (the speck tile), and -0.019575 on blobs, which
  reproduces the owner's quoted -33.76 / -0.0196 pair exactly. It is orientation-invariant, as the
  corrected test asserts: stripe_x and stripe_y both give -33.761250 to the last digit.
- **A2** moves: range 6.791986 over the eight tiles, from -3.395993 (stripe_y) to +3.395993
  (stripe_x). Blobs (-0.911524), white noise (+0.008949) and the 16 px mosaic (-0.785466) are all
  distinct, so it is not constant. Note the hard bound: `_efold` returns `len(ac)` = 128 when the
  autocorrelation never falls below 1/e, so |A2| can never exceed `log(128/1)` = 4.852; stripe_x's
  3.396 is 70% of the way to that ceiling. A2 is a saturated statistic by construction.
- **A3** moves: range 0.984375, and the underlying variogram crossing is a real lag measurement
  (1 px for white noise, 2 px for stripes, 14 px for the 16 px mosaic, 51 px for blobs, 116 px for
  the ramp). Finding: A3 is quantised. `h[hit]` is an integer lag count and the ppm cancels, so A3
  is exactly `hit_lag / 128` for a 256 px tile; its resolution is one step = 0.0078125. Stripe vs
  noise differ by exactly one step (0.015625 vs 0.007812), which is why the sanity check in the
  contract compares the 16 px mosaic against noise and against the 3 px mosaic rather than stripes
  against noise.
- **A4** moves: range 0.335853, dominated by the negative side (-0.333333 on stripes). The two
  terms are printed so the difference is auditable. On the speck tile both terms are 0.0 because
  the mask (25 px) contains no pair 5 px apart in either direction: A4 collapses to exactly 0.0
  rather than signalling "undefined". Same value 0.0 arises from a completely different cause on
  stripe_y and on the ramp, where both continuity terms are equal by symmetry. 0.0 is therefore
  not a reliable degeneracy flag for A4.

### 2.4 Error paths: degenerate mask, bad ppm, bad shape

From the passing run above:

- degenerate mask: `AssertionError: degenerate mask: only 0 pixels survive the 12th pct` for a flat

- ppm = 0.0, -1.0, -0.0001: `AssertionError: ppm must be positive, got <value>` (3 checks).
- ppm = `None`: `TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'`,
  raised by `float(ppm)` before the positivity test. Accepted as a raise by the contract.
- ppm = `nan`: `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer`, from
  `lag_px = int(round(A4_LAG_MM * ppm))`. Note the ordering: `mask_and_field` alone does **not**
  reject NaN ppm (`max(0.5, nan/k)` inside `_illumination_base` silently becomes 0.5), so a NaN
  scale only surfaces later, and with an unhelpful message. It cannot pass silently, which is the
  requirement, but it does not fail at the argument boundary.
- 2D tile (32, 32): `AssertionError: expected HxWx3 tile, got (32, 32)`.
- ppm < 0.5 (below the physically possible range here): `lag_px` rounds to 0 and `_continuity`

**Owner instruction on registration:** register M7-A first; keep the exact frozen K = 4 feature

unless M7-A is rejected by its pre-gates or fails G1.

**Hypothesis H7-A.** Some of the remaining internal CV error is carried by spatial *organisation*
of texture inside a tile - directionality and scale-free continuity - which the 12 features cannot
represent because each is a permutation-invariant summary of a tile's masked pixel multiset
(`preprocess/verify.py:105-128`; tile->image and image->soil aggregation are two plain per-column
medians). Adding four such statistics as frozen-pipeline inputs lowers family-honest internal CV EMD.

**Data source.** Existing materialised 256 px tiles and `manifest_tiles.csv`
(`tile_x, tile_y, grid_col, grid_row, tile_w_mm`). Tiles are *read*, never regenerated;
`data/Training`, `data/Test`, `data/processed_meta` are not modified; no preprocessing is re-run.
1946 qualifying tiles (soil_fraction >= 0.50, materialized), 1541 train / 405 test split.

**The four statistics, fixed now, K = 4 columns.** Computed per tile on the mask-interior grey field
`g` and the band-pass residual `e` already defined in preprocessing; then aggregated by the same
median rules as the existing 12.

their approved wording to state one measurement each, unambiguously. Nothing else in this

def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global TOTAL
    TOTAL += 1
    print("%-6s %s%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, (" | " + detail) if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        FAIL.append(name)


def caught(fn, *args, **kw):
    """The exception a call raises, or None. Checks assert on the TYPE, which is the whole point of
    the ruling's split: knowing that something raised does not tell TileDegenerate from
    ValueError."""
    try:
        fn(*args, **kw)
    except Exception as exc:
        return exc
    return None


def noisy(fn, *args, **kw):
    """Call fn with every warning recorded instead of raised, and keep what happened.

    Returns (result, exception_or_None, ["Category: message", ...]). The three-part return exists
    because a check that looks only at the warning list can pass while the call raises, so every
    caller below is asked to assert on the exception slot too - that omission was itself a review
    finding in fix round 2.

    It is used on the statistic path (to prove it is silent), on the aggregation path (to catch the
    ONE deliberate all-NaN notice, which is a warning by design), and on the new undefined-statistic
    probes, where raising TileDegenerate is the expected outcome and must not be confused with a
    number. It never suppresses anything: the records are handed back to the caller, and the
    runner's simplefilter("error") is still in force for every check that does not call this.
    """
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as got:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        res, err = None, None
        try:
            res = fn(*args, **kw)
        except Exception as exc:
            err = exc
    return res, err, [w.category.__name__ + ": " + str(w.message) for w in got]

**Status: APPROVED AND FROZEN 2026-09-29 by the owner. Registered as Model 7 / Experiment 1.**

**Nothing below was reworded, re-thresholded or re-parameterised when it moved here.** It is the
approved pre-registration text, relocated verbatim so this folder is the single source of truth for
M7-A. Section 1 (boundary rulings) and section 3 (the unrun M7-C pre-registration) stay in

definition, the alias-separability gate, the controls, the family-honest LOFO protocol, the G0 anchor
43.0217308796477 and the G1 >= 3.00 EMD threshold unchanged; do not submit unless the pre-registered
criteria are satisfied; no tuning, feature expansion, or post-hoc selection after seeing the CV
result. M7-T stays suspended; M7-B and M7-E are not revived; M7-C stays preregistered and unrun
unless M7-A is rejected by its pre-gates or fails G1.

---


**Hypothesis H7-A.** Some of the remaining internal CV error is carried by spatial *organisation*
of texture inside a tile - directionality and scale-free continuity - which the 12 features cannot
represent because each is a permutation-invariant summary of a tile's masked pixel multiset
(`preprocess/verify.py:105-128`; tile->image and image->soil aggregation are two plain per-column
medians). Adding four such statistics as frozen-pipeline inputs lowers family-honest internal CV EMD.

**Data source.** Existing materialised 256 px tiles and `manifest_tiles.csv`
(`tile_x, tile_y, grid_col, grid_row, tile_w_mm`). Tiles are *read*, never regenerated;
`data/Training`, `data/Test`, `data/processed_meta` are not modified; no preprocessing is re-run.
1946 qualifying tiles (soil_fraction >= 0.50, materialized), 1541 train / 405 test split.

**The four statistics, fixed now, K = 4 columns.** Computed per tile on the mask-interior grey field
`g` and the band-pass residual `e` already defined in preprocessing; then aggregated by the same
median rules as the existing 12.

**AMENDMENT 1 - owner-authorized, 2026-09-29, before Task 2.** The three cells below were amended from
their approved wording to state one measurement each, unambiguously. Nothing else in this
pre-registration changed: the hypothesis, K = 4, the four statistic *ids and roles*, the controls, the
protocol, gates G0-G7, the 3.00 EMD bar and the submission rule are exactly as approved. The owner
ruled on four divergences that the Task 1 review found between this text and the plan's code; each
ruling is recorded with the original wording preserved verbatim underneath it, and the pre-amendment
text is also preserved in the repository history. The A1 cell is unchanged.

| id | definition | why the 12 cannot express it |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **structure-tensor anisotropy** `log((lambda2 + eps) / (lambda1 + eps))` of `(gx, gy)` over masked pixels, lambda1 >= lambda2 | `grad_mean` is `hypot(gx,gy)` magnitude only; orientation is never used |
| A2 | **autocorrelation e-folding length ratio** `L(0 deg) / L(90 deg)` of the residual `e`, each length measured in mm along its own profile. A **plain ratio, not a log-ratio.** A profile line lying wholly outside the mask is **skipped**, never substituted by 0.0; if every line in a direction is masked out, A2 is **undefined** for that tile. """Contract test for spatial_features.py. Run: python check_spatial_features.py"""
import ast
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import spatial_features as sf  # noqa: E402

FAIL = []
TOTAL = 0
PPM = 4.552516  # the canonical tile scale; every mm quantity below is derived from it


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global TOTAL
    TOTAL += 1
    print("%-6s %s%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, (" | " + detail) if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        FAIL.append(name)


def raises(fn, *args, **kw):
    """Return (raised, exception_name, message). The contract below is that it must raise."""
    try:
        fn(*args, **kw)
    except Exception as exc:
        return True, type(exc).__name__, str(exc)
    return False, "", ""


def striped(width=256, height=256, period=8):
    """A tile with stripes along x: strongly anisotropic, and orientation-flippable.

    The broadcast_to is not decoration: `128.0 + 40.0 * cos(...)` has shape (H, 1), and dstack of
    three (H, 1) arrays gives (H, 1, 3), on which np.gradient raises "Shape of array too small".
    Verified 2026-09-29 while checking this task before dispatch.
    """
    y = np.arange(height)[:, None]
    row = 128.0 + 40.0 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * (y % period) / period)
    g = np.broadcast_to(row, (height, width)).copy()
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def blobs(seed=0, size=24):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    a = np.full((256, 256, 3), 120.0)
    for _ in range(30):
        cy, cx = rng.integers(0, 256, 2)
        yy, xx = np.ogrid[:256, :256]
        m = ((yy - cy) ** 2 + (xx - cx) ** 2) <= (size / 2) ** 2
        a[m] += 60.0
    return a


def grain_noise(seed=3):
    """White pixel noise: no lateral correlation at any lag beyond one pixel."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256, 256, 3))


def coarse_blocks(seed=4, block=16):
    """A 16 px mosaic: correlation length set by the block, not by the pixel."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    small = rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256 // block, 256 // block))
    g = np.kron(small, np.ones((block, block)))
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def fine_grains(seed=5, block=3):
    """The same mosaic recipe at 3 px: much shorter correlation length than block 16."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    small = rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256 // block, 256 // block))
    g = np.kron(small, np.ones((block, block)))
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def speck_on_dark(side=5):
    """Mask survives as one 5x5 island, so no masked pair is 5 px apart at 4.55 px/mm.

    This is the degenerate-lag-pair-set case: A4's numerator has zero pairs and the statistic
    collapses to exactly 0.0 rather than moving with any texture.
    """
    a = np.full((256, 256, 3), 10.0)
    a[40:40 + side, 70:70 + side] = 230.0
    return a


def ramp(width=256, height=256):
    """A monotone linear grey ramp: an exactly rank-1 gradient field.

    This is the boundary case for A1's eigenvalue floor. tr/2 - sqrt(disc) evaluates to zero (up
    to roundoff) when every gradient vector is parallel, so it is the only synthetic tile here that
    exercises max(..., 0.0) rather than sailing past it.
    """
    g = np.linspace(0.0, 255.0, width)[None, :]
    g = np.broadcast_to(g, (height, width)).copy()
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def value_table(tiles):
    """{name: statistic dict} for the mutation sanity checks, one tile_spatial call per tile."""
    return {name: sf.tile_spatial(a, PPM) for name, a in tiles.items()}


def spread(values, key):
    got = [v[key] for v in values.values()]
    return max(got) - min(got), got


def fmt(values, key):
    return "; ".join("%s=%.6f" % (n, v[key]) for n, v in values.items())


# Golden reference values, measured from the frozen module on 2026-09-29 at PPM = 4.552516 and
# asserted at max(5% relative, 0.02 absolute). Same device preprocess/verify.py uses for the 12.
# The invariance and "can this statistic move" checks are blind to a change that moves all tiles
# together; this table is not. It was added after mutation testing found that replacing _acf_along's
# zero-fill of fully masked rows/columns with neighbour interpolation escapes every other check
# (it shifts A2 on blobs by 0.334, which no separation threshold sees).

    "blobs": {"A1": -0.019575082103750408, "A2": -0.9115238226701586,
              "A3": 0.39843750000000006, "A4": -0.0152100924327454},

                 "A3": 0.109375, "A4": -0.11221709712903871},
}
GOLDEN_TILES = {"blobs": blobs, "stripe_x": striped, "noise": grain_noise,
                "coarse16": coarse_blocks}


def test_golden_values_reproduced():
    for name, maker in GOLDEN_TILES.items():
        out = sf.tile_spatial(maker(), PPM)
        for key in sf.SPATIAL:
            want, got = GOLDEN[name][key], out[key]
            tol = max(0.05 * abs(want), 0.02)
            check("%s %s within max(5%%, 0.02) of golden" % (name, key),
                  abs(got - want) <= tol, "want %.6f got %.6f tol %.6f" % (want, got, tol))

def test_returns_four_keys_in_order():
    out = sf.tile_spatial(striped(), 4.552516)
    check("returns exactly A1-A4", tuple(out) == sf.SPATIAL, str(tuple(out)))
    check("all four are finite floats",
          all(isinstance(v, float) and np.isfinite(v) for v in out.values()))

def caught(fn, *args, **kw):
    """The exception a call raises, or None. Checks assert on the TYPE, which is the whole point of
    the ruling's split: `raises` alone cannot tell TileDegenerate from ValueError."""
    try:
        fn(*args, **kw)
    except Exception as exc:
        return exc
    return None


def raises(fn, *args, **kw):
    """Return (raised, exception_name, message). The contract below is that it must raise."""
    exc = caught(fn, *args, **kw)
    if exc is None:
        return False, "", ""
    return True, type(exc).__name__, str(exc)


def noisy(fn, *args, **kw):
    """Call fn with every warning recorded instead of raised.

    Returns (result, exception_or_None, ["Category: message", ...]). Used twice: to prove the
    statistic path is silent, and to catch the ONE deliberate notice in the aggregation. Any other
    use of this helper would be a way of silencing a warning, which the ruling forbids, so it is
    never used around tile_spatial's assertions.
    """
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as got:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        res, err = None, None
        try:
            res = fn(*args, **kw)
        except Exception as exc:
            err = exc
    return res, err, [w.category.__name__ + ": " + str(w.message) for w in got]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- synthetic tiles
def striped(width=256, height=256, period=8):
    """A tile with stripes along x: strongly anisotropic, and orientation-flippable.

    The broadcast_to is not decoration: `128.0 + 40.0 * cos(...)` has shape (H, 1), and dstack of
    three (H, 1) arrays gives (H, 1, 3), on which np.gradient raises "Shape of array too small".
    Verified 2026-09-29 while checking this task before dispatch.
    """
    y = np.arange(height)[:, None]
    row = 128.0 + 40.0 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * (y % period) / period)
    g = np.broadcast_to(row, (height, width)).copy()
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def blobs(seed=0, size=24):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    a = np.full((256, 256, 3), 120.0)
    for _ in range(30):
        cy, cx = rng.integers(0, 256, 2)
        yy, xx = np.ogrid[:256, :256]
        m = ((yy - cy) ** 2 + (xx - cx) ** 2) <= (size / 2) ** 2
        a[m] += 60.0
    return a


def grain_noise(seed=3):
    """White pixel noise: no lateral correlation at any lag beyond one pixel."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256, 256, 3))


def coarse_blocks(seed=4, block=16):
    """A 16 px mosaic: correlation length set by the block, not by the pixel."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    small = rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256 // block, 256 // block))
    g = np.kron(small, np.ones((block, block)))
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])


def fine_grains(seed=5, block=3):
    """The same mosaic recipe at 3 px: much shorter correlation length than block 16."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    small = rng.uniform(60.0, 200.0, (256 // block, 256 // block))
    g = np.kron(small, np.ones((block, block)))
    return np.dstack([g, g, g])

Also need to mention "Is bin resolution redundant with digit decomposition, or complementary?" — evidence: Deotte's S5E2 solution uses digit/rounding features at default bins and won; the mechanism per docs is that a single exact value is unrepresentable in 255 bins, and sklearn HistGB hard-caps at 255 → digit/TE route works everywhere; raising max_bin gets you partway (a tree can isolate narrow intervals) but needs ~log2(bins) splits and only helps if the value's neighbourhood is informative. So complementary in that they attack the same quantization bottleneck; TE/digits are strictly more expressive for lookup-style signals, while max_bin helps smooth thresholds. The setup\n\nLet $s_i \\\\in \\\\mathbb{R}^n$ be the predictions of file $i$ on the $n = 286{,}571$ test rows, and let\n$a_i$ be its **measured public ROC-AUC** (given in the catalog, exact to five decimals).\n\nRank-transform each file to a Gaussian score, $g_i = \\\\Phi^{-1}\\\\!\\\\big(\\\\mathrm{rank}(s_i)/(n+1)\\\\big)$.\nAUC is invariant to monotone transforms, so $a_i$ is unchanged, but now every file has the\nsame marginal scale and calibration differences disappear.\n\nAssume the usual **binormal, equal-variance** model on the scored (public) rows:\n\n$$g_i \\\\mid y{=}1 \\\\sim \\\\mathcal{N}(\\\\mu_{1i}, \\\\sigma_i^2), \\\\qquad\n  g_i \\\\mid y{=}0 \\\\sim \\\\mathcal{N}(\\\\mu_{0i}, \\\\sigma_i^2).$$\n\nThen $a_i = \\\\Phi\\\\!\\\\big(\\\\delta_i / (\\\\sigma_i\\\\sqrt{2})\\\\big)$ with $\\\\delta_i = \\\\mu_{1i}-\\\\mu_{0i}$.\nWrite $z_i \\\\equiv \\\\sqrt{2}\\\\,\\\\Phi^{-1}(a_i) = \\\\delta_i/\\\\sigma_i$. Because $g_i$ is standard normal\n*marginally*, its pooled variance is $1 = \\\\sigma_i^2 + \\\\pi(1-\\\\pi)\\\\delta_i^2$, so\n\n$$\\\\boxed{\\\\;\\\\delta_i \\\\;=\\\\; \\\\frac{z_i}{\\\\sqrt{1+\\\\pi(1-\\\\pi)z_i^{2}}}\\\\;,\\\\qquad z_i=\\\\sqrt2\\\\,\\\\Phi^{-1}(a_i)\\\\;}$$\n\nwith $\\\\pi$ the positive rate. **Each public score is converted into one coordinate of $\\\\delta$.**\n\n## 2. Why we never need the labels\n\nFor a blend $f = w^\\\\top g$, the same binormal algebra gives\n\n$$\\\\mathrm{AUC}(w) \\\\;=\\\\; \\\\Phi\\\\!\\\\left(\\\\frac{w^\\\\top \\\\delta}{\\\\sqrt{2}\\\\,\\\\sqrt{w^\\\\top \\\\Sigma_W w}}\\\\right),$$\n\nwhich is maximized by the Fisher direction $w \\\\propto \\\\Sigma_W^{-1}\\\\delta$, where $\\\\Sigma_W$ is the\n**within-class** covariance — which we cannot compute, because it needs labels.\n\nBut the **pooled** covariance $\\\\Sigma_P$ (computable from the test predictions alone) satisfies\n$\\\\Sigma_P = \\\\Sigma_W + \\\\pi(1-\\\\pi)\\\\,\\\\delta\\\\delta^\\\\top$. By Sherman–Morrison,\n\n$$\\\\Sigma_P^{-1}\\\\delta \\\\;=\\\\; \\\\frac{\\\\Sigma_W^{-1}\\\\delta}{1+\\\\pi(1-\\\\pi)\\\\,\\\\delta^\\\\top\\\\Sigma_W^{-1}\\\\delta}\n\\\\;\\\\;\\\\propto\\\\;\\\\; \\\\Sigma_W^{-1}\\\\delta .$$\n\nThe rank-one class term only rescales the solution; **the direction is identical**. So the\nlabel-free pooled covariance of the unlabeled test predictions is *sufficient*. That is the one\nstep that makes this practical.\n\n## 3. What it does that top-K averaging does not\n\nScore-weighted averaging treats a file\u0027s public AUC as its value. $\\\\Sigma^{-1}\\\\delta$ instead asks\nwhat each file adds *conditional on all the others*. Ten near-duplicate copies of the same blend\nget the weight of one; a mediocre but genuinely different model (a logistic regression, a RealMLP)\ncan get a large weight because it is the only one carrying its direction. ### (2) Feature List & Engineering
**Base Features (`FEATURES`)**
- Numeric: `Age`, `Annual_Income_USD`, `Daily_Commute_km`, `Number_of_Cars_Owned`, `Charging_Stations_Near_Home`, `Charging_Stations_Near_Work`, `Environmental_Concern_Level`
- Categorical: `Gender`, `City_Type`, `Current_Car_Type`, `Home_Charging_Possible`, `Subsidy_Available`, `Range_Anxiety_Level`

**Derived / Label-Free (`BASE_COLS`)**
- Ordinal mappings for categoricals
- Income digit extractions: `inc_d0` … `inc_d5`
- Floor flags: `inc_is_min` (income==30k), `commute_is_min` (commute==5km)
- Frequency counts (trained on train+test): `cnt_inc`, `cnt_com`

**Target Encoding (OOF-safe, computed per outer fold)**
| Feature | Key | Smooth Prior (`m`) | Notes |
|---------|-----|-------------------|-------|
| `te_inc` | exact income | 1.0 | Exploits synthetic income artifact |
| `te_inc_s20` | exact income | 20.0 | Smoother variant (XGB/LR/MLP) |
| `te_com` | commute ×10 | 20.0 | |
| `te_age` | age | 20.0 | |
| `te_inc10` | income ÷10 | 20.0 | Groups nearby incomes |
| `wte_30` | window ±30 USD | 5.0 | Excludes self; captures local neighborhood |

All TE values are calibrated inside the outer fold using an inner 5-fold scheme to prevent target leakage.

### (3) Cross-Validation & AUC Scores
- **Fold Scheme**: `StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)`. Identical folds used across all models to ensure honest stacking.
- **Adversarial Validation**: Train vs Test classifier AUC ≈ `0.5000` → confirms identical distributions; local CV reliably predicts leaderboard.
- **Internal CV AUCs** (reported in notebook):

| LightGBM (rich) | 0.94587 |
| **Ensemble (Stacking + Nested CV)** | **0.94605** |

### (4) Blending Weights & Post-Processing (Verbatim)
```python
def to_logit(p):
    return logit(np.clip(np.asarray(p, dtype=np.float64), 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))

O = np.column_stack([to_logit(RESULTS[n]["oof"]) for n in names])
T = np.column_stack([to_logit(RESULTS[n]["test"]) for n in names])

def hill_climb(X, yy, iters=50, tol=1e-6):
    """Caruana: adiciona (com reposição) o modelo que mais melhora o AUC da média."""
    scores = [roc_auc_score(yy, X[:, j]) for j in range(X.shape[1])]
    counts = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
    j0 = int(np.argmax(scores))
    counts[j0], cur, cur_s = 1, X[:, j0].copy(), scores[j0]
    for _ in range(iters):
        n = counts.sum()
        s, j = max((roc_auc_score(yy, (cur * n + X[:, j]) / (n + 1)), j) for j in range(X.shape[1]))
        if s - cur_s < tol:
            break
        cur, cur_s = (cur * n + X[:, j]) / (n + 1), s
        counts[j] += 1
    return counts / counts.sum()

def nested(method):
    pred = np.zeros(len(y))
    for k in range(N_SPLITS):
        tr, va = folds != k, folds == k
        if method == "média":
            pred[va] = O[va].mean(1)
        elif method == "hill climbing":
            pred[va] = O[va] @ hill_climb(O[tr], y[tr])
        else:
            pred[va] = LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=2000).fit(O[tr], y[tr]).decision_function(O[va])
    return roc_auc_score(y, pred)

ens_scores = {m: nested(m) for m in ["média", "hill climbing", "stacking (LogReg)"]}
best_method = max(ens_scores, key=ens_scores.get)
if best_method == "média":
    w = np.full(len(names), 1 / len(names))
    oof_score, test_score = O @ w, T @ w
elif best_method == "hill climbing":
    w = hill_climb(O, y)
    oof_score, test_score = O @ w, T @ w
else:
    stk = LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=2000).fit(O, y)
    w = stk.coef_.ravel()
    oof_score, test_score = stk.decision_function(O), stk.decision_function(T)
final_pred = expit(test_score)
```
Weights `w` are output as `pd.Series(w, index=names, name="peso").round(4).to_frame()` and applied to the averaged test predictions before sigmoid calibration.

**Hypothesis H7-A.** Some of the remaining internal CV error is carried by spatial *organisation*
of texture inside a tile - directionality and scale-free continuity - which the 12 features cannot
represent because each is a permutation-invariant summary of a tile's masked pixel multiset
(`preprocess/verify.py:105-128`; tile->image and image->soil aggregation are two plain per-column
medians). Adding four such statistics as frozen-pipeline inputs lowers family-honest internal CV EMD.

**Data source.** Existing materialised 256 px tiles and `manifest_tiles.csv`
(`tile_x, tile_y, grid_col, grid_row, tile_w_mm`). Tiles are *read*, never regenerated;
`data/Training`, `data/Test`, `data/processed_meta` are not modified; no preprocessing is re-run.
1946 qualifying tiles (soil_fraction >= 0.50, materialized), 1541 train / 405 test split.

**The four statistics, fixed now, K = 4 columns.** Computed per tile on the mask-interior grey field
`g` and the band-pass residual `e` already defined in preprocessing; then aggregated by the same
median rules as the existing 12.

(0.932 mm); 4 px would give 1.242 mm, so 3 px is the ruling and the residual mismatch is stated
rather than smoothed over.

1. Three-way separation. Let me trace:
- `compute_tile_row` calls `sf.tile_spatial` directly; only `classify_tile` catches `sf.TileDegenerate`. So an unexpected exception (ValueError from ppm<=0, or any other) propagates out of classify_tile, out of the `for` loop in scan_tiles, and the `finally` records it as an abort via `_record_abort` and re-raises (propagates naturally since we're not catching).
- Important: `scan_tiles` uses `try: ... finally:` — with `sys.exc_info()[1]` in the finally. Careful: `sys.exc_info()` inside a `finally` block of a `try` that had no `except`: during exception propagation, sys.exc_info() returns the in-flight exception in CPython. Yes, that works. But there's a subtlety: `warnings.catch_warnings()` context manager... the finally of the outer try runs after the with block exits. sys.exc_info() should still be the in-flight exception. Hmm — actually the exception propagates through `__exit__` of catch_warnings first; catch_warnings' __exit__ doesn't catch the exception (it doesn't return True; it just restores), so sys.exc_info() would still be set. Actually, when an exception propagates through a `with` block, Python calls `__exit__(type, val, tb)` and during that call sys.exc_info() returns the exception. After the with block exits, the exception continues propagating out of the try body, and the finally clause runs while the exception is in flight → sys.exc_info() returns it. That should work; the test `test_invalid_call_aborts_and_is_never_counted_as_degeneracy` verifies the errors list is populated, and it's reported passing (150/0). So the recording path does work — for the ValueError case.
- However: does the `finally` mislabel anything? The recording happens on ANY exception escaping, including... KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit (BaseException) — `_record_abort(ctx, exc)` typed as BaseException, fine. But also: the `finally` records an error whenever an exception escapes the body, even when it's not from a tile call. E.g. `tile_table(root)` is called BEFORE the try, so fine.
- One real issue: `ctx["current"]` is set AFTER the missing-tile check; the missing-tile AssertionError records `cur.get("tile_path")` from ctx["current"] which is stale from a previous tile if the missing tile is not the first! Let's look: in the loop,
```
path = root / r.tile_path
if not path.exists():
    raise AssertionError(...)
ctx["current"] = {...}
```

## Route Takeaway

With weights frozen, everything this route can do is **condition** a pretrained function on new inputs: retrieve passages into context (RAG/kNN-LM/RETRO/Memorizing Transformers), take a nearest-class-mean over a frozen embedding space (prototypes, CLIP zero-shot, LP-FT), or store executable programs and prompts outside the network (Voyager, Reflexion, FunSearch/AlphaEvolve) — and the strongest verified gains are real but bounded (RETRO matching a 25×-larger model with 2% of the parameters and a 2T-token datastore; Voyager's lifelong skill library giving 3.3× more items and 15.3× faster milestones with *no* fine-tuning; FunSearch finding previously unknown mathematics with no backprop at all). The route stops working exactly at the point where the new material requires a **new function rather than a new lookup**: retrieval supplies facts (recital), while k-hop derivations from newly read facts degrade with reasoning depth and knowledge scale, and inverted or compositional versions of a fact the model "knows" from context collapse (the reversal curse; NeurIPS 2025's RANK testbed). The few-shot perception half fails for a different reason: prototype/linear-probe transfer is nearly free *only because someone already paid for the structure* — contrastive or supervised training that made the target class linearly separable — so 5 dog photos work because ImageNet-scale geometry exists, and the same recipe on a genuinely novel category, modality or symbol system has nothing to interpolate. Finally, the "learning" is relocated, not eliminated: capacity moves into the retriever's encoder and index (capped by ~2 bits/parameter if you ever do want it inside weights), cost moves into ever-growing stores and per-query search, and the verifier/search loop of evolutionary synthesis just moves gradient descent into an expensive outer loop that produces domain-specific artifacts, not transferable competence.

## Sources

[50] Yunzhi Yao, Ningyu Zhang, Zekun Xi, Mengru Wang, Ziwen Xu, Shumin Deng, Huajun Chen — "Knowledge Circuits in Pretrained Transformers" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17969 — NeurIPS 2024 (26 pp., submitted 28 May 2024) — Tier 1
Summary: Knowledge is instantiated as a sparse *subnetwork* (information heads + relation heads + MLPs), verified on GPT-2 and TinyLLaMA. Consequence for this route: context/retrieval can only *reactivate* circuits that pretraining already built; knowledge-editing methods that try to bolt facts on damage the circuits and the model's general ability — which is why editing is "brittle, only works in narrow cases" per the authors' own evaluation.
Key quotes: "we delve into the computation graph of the language model to uncover the knowledge circuits that are instrumental in articulating specific knowledge"; "we utilize knowledge circuits to analyze and interpret language model behaviors such as hallucinations and in-context learning."

[51] Harshay Shah, Badih Ghazi, Yangsibo Huang, Ravi Kumar, Da Yu, Chiyuan Zhang (Google Research) — "Do Language Models Robustly Acquire New Knowledge?" — https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/123879 — NeurIPS 2025 — Tier 1
Summary: The cleanest 2025 negative result *for* the retrieval route. Introduces **RANK**, a principled testbed for new-knowledge acquisition that separates simple recall from *k-hop reasoning over newly supplied facts*, and compares in-context/retrieval injection against SFT. Retrieval-based acquisition is the one that degrades: ICL performance falls off as reasoning complexity and the scale of injected knowledge grow, while SFT on simple facts "fails completely" at multi-hop — i.e. neither pure-read nor shallow-train gives derived capability.
Key quotes: "ICL performance degrades with reasoning complexity and knowledge scale"; "SFT trained on simple facts fails completely at multi-hop reasoning"; data diversity induces generalization transitions. (No percentages in the abstract — worth pulling from the PDF.)

[52] Zeyuan (Allen-Zhu), Yuanzhi Li (Microsoft Research) — "Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3, Knowledge Capacity Scaling Laws" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405 — arXiv 8 Apr 2024 (companion to Parts 3.1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.14316 and 3.2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.14402) — Tier 1
Summary: The capacity ceiling that motivates *and* limits weight-free memory: a model stores only ~2 bits of knowledge per parameter even at int8 quantization, so a 7B model holds ~14B bits (more than English Wikipedia + textbooks combined). Part 3.2's practical finding is the honest version of "learning from docs": an "onboarding" format (document-style, knowledge-adjacent pretraining-like presentation) accelerates acquisition of new knowledge dramatically — but only when the target facts are *composable with knowledge the model already has*; genuinely alien functions stay unlearnable. (The frequently-quoted "~650× more knowledge" figure is from Part 3.2 — verify the exact multiplier against the paper before citing.)
Key quotes: "language models can and only can store 2 bits of knowledge per parameter, even when quantized to int8"; "a 7B model can store 14B bits of knowledge … surpassing the English Wikipedia and textbooks combined."

[53] Urvashi Khandelwal, Angela Fan, Dan Jurafsky, Luke Zettlemoyer, Mike Lewis — "Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00438 — ICLR 2020; earlier capped-memory version https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00177 (Findings of EMNLP 2020) — Tier 1
Summary: The canonical "memory outside the weights" result: interpolate LM output with a kNN over a datastore of cached (context → next-token) pairs. Perplexity improves and a model can *adapt to a new domain or task by swapping the datastore, with zero gradient updates* — this is the strongest evidence that frozen weights + external memory can change behavior. The boundary is that the datastore indexes the *encoder's own* representations: it can only surface distributions the froze

def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    global TOTAL
    TOTAL += 1
    print("%-6s %s%s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, (" | " + detail) if detail else ""))
    if not ok:
        FAIL.append(name)


def caught(fn, *args, **kw):
    """The exception a call raises, or None. Checks assert on the TYPE, which is the whole point of
    the ruling's split: knowing that something raised does not tell TileDegenerate from ValueError."""
    try:
        fn(*args, **kw)
    except Exception as exc:
        return exc
    return None


def noisy(fn, *args, **kw):
    """Call fn with every warning recorded instead of raised.

    Returns (result, exception_or_None, ["Category: message", ...]). Used twice: to prove the
    statistic path is silent, and to catch the ONE deliberate notice in the aggregation. Any other
    use of this helper would be a way of silencing a warning, which the ruling forbids, so it is
    never used around tile_spatial's assertions.
    """
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as got:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        res, err = None, None
        try:
            res = fn(*args, **kw)
        except Exception as exc:
            err = exc
    return res, err, [w.category.__name__ + ": " + str(w.message) for w in got]

import os, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=None
D="data"; EXT={".jpg",".jpeg",".png"}
lab=pd.read_csv("data/Training_labels_updated.csv").set_index("sample_id")
dl=np.log10([0.002,0.0063,0.02,0.063,0.2,0.63,2,6.3,20,63,200])
PPM={"MotorolaEdge":11.492*0.4,"SamsungA52":26.33*(1599/9248),"MotEdge60Fusion":12.465,
     "iPhone14":13.942,"iPhone16":19.525}
def cam(f,s=""):
    fl=f.lower()
    if "samsung" in fl: return "SamsungA52"
    if "fusion" in fl: return "MotEdge60Fusion"
    if "motorola" in fl: return "MotorolaEdge"
    if "iphone14" in fl or "iphone_14" in fl: return "iPhone14"
    return "iPhone16"
def feats(path,ppm,target_ppm=4.58):
    im=Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    w,h=im.size
    # normalize to a common physical scale so px <-> mm is identical for every camera
    s=target_ppm/ppm
    nw,nh=max(int(w*s),32),max(int(h*s),32)
    im=im.resize((nw,nh)); g=np.asarray(im.convert("L"),float)
    dark=g<np.percentile(g,8)
    base=ndi.gaussian_filter(g,min(nh,nw)//12)
    e=g-base
    m=g>np.percentile(g,12)
    out={"darkfrac":float(dark.mean()),"bright":float(g[m].mean()),"logD50":0}
    for sc in [1,2,4,8,16,32]:
        b=ndi.gaussian_filter(np.where(m,e,0),sc)
        out[f"e{sc}"]=float(np.sqrt(b[m].var()+1e-12))
    a=np.asarray(im,float)[m]
    out["R"],out["G"],out["B"]=[float(a[:,k].mean()) for k in range(3)]
    out["sat"]=float((a.max(1)-a.min(1)).mean()/(a.mean()+1e-6))
    out["px_per_mm"]=target_ppm; out["delivered_px"]=f"{w}x{h}"; out["fov_mm"]=f"{w/ppm:.0f}x{h/ppm:.0f}"
    return out
rows=[]
for split,root,idx in [("train",os.path.join(D,"Training"),lab.index),("test",os.path.join(D,"Test"),None)]:
    for s in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        p=os.path.join(root,s)
        if not os.path.isdir(p): continue
        fs=[f for f in sorted(os.listdir(p)) if os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower() in EXT]
        per=[]
        for f in fs:
            c=cam(f); per.append(dict(feats(os.path.join(p,f),PPM[c]),cam=c,n_of_imgs=len(fs)))
        df=pd.DataFrame(per)
        r=df.mean(numeric_only=True).to_dict()
        r["cam_mix"]=dict(df.cam.value_counts()); r["split"]=split
        r["key"]=s; rows.append(r)
F=pd.DataFrame(rows)
F.to_csv("_look/all_features.csv",index=False)
print("=== per-image FOV spread within a sample (scale consistency check) ===")
for split in ["train","test"]:
    sub=F[F.split==split]
    print(f" {split}: samples={len(sub)}")
print("\n=== TEST SAMPLES ===")
print(F[F.split=="test"][["key","cam_mix","delivered_px","fov_mm","e1","e2","e4","e8","e16","e32","bright","R","B","sat","darkfrac"]].to_string(index=False))
print("\n=== TRAIN (sorted by D50) ===")
tr=F[F.split=="train"].copy()
tr["logD50"]=[np.interp(50,np.maximum(lab.loc[k].to_numpy(float),np.linspace(1e-6,1,11)),dl) for k in tr.key]
print(tr.sort_values("logD50")[["key","cam_mix","fov_mm","e1","e4","e16","e32","bright","sat","darkfrac","logD50"]].to_string(index=False))
print("\n=== nearest train neighbour for each test sample (DoG feature space, standardized) ===")
cols=["e1","e2","e4","e8","e16","e32","bright","R","G","B","sat","darkfrac"]
Xtr=tr[cols].to_numpy(float); mu,sd=Xtr.mean(0),Xtr.std(0)+1e-9
Xtr=(Xtr-mu)/sd
for _,r in F[F.split=="test"].iterrows():
    z=(r[cols].to_numpy(float)-mu)/sd
    d=np.linalg.norm(Xtr-z,axis=1); o=np.argsort(d)[:3]
    print(f"  {r['key']:28s} -> "+", ".join(f"{tr.key.values[i]}(D50={10**tr.logD50.values[i]:.3f}mm,d={d[i]:.1f})" for i in o))
EOF

Read the whole thing, bro. Here's where you actually stand — and three of the findings change the plan.

## What the competition is

Predict a soil's cumulative grain-size curve at 11 fixed diameters (0.002→200 mm) from photos of soil spread in a dark tray. Scored by log-weighted Earth Mover's Distance = **the area between the true and predicted curve when plotted against log₁₀(diameter)**. Range 0–500, lower is better. Hosted by BOKU's GRID project; $500, 366 participants, ~2 months left.

## The three findings that matter most

**1. Your `information.md` PPM table is wrong for the pixels you actually have.**

The CSV quotes PPM at each camera's *native* resolution — but the training images were downscaled before release. Motorola Edge ships as 1600×720 (native 4000×1800, ×0.4) and the Samsung A52 as 1599×1200 (native 9248×6936, ×0.173). Correcting for that:

| camera | images | real px/mm in the file | smallest grain you can see |
|---|---|---|---|
| Motorola Edge | 69 | **4.60** | ~0.87 mm |
| Samsung A52 | 55 | **4.55** | ~0.88 mm |
| Edge 60 Fusion (H374 only) | 3 | **12.47** | 0.32 mm |
| iPhone 14 (test) | 14 | **13.94** | 0.29 mm |
| iPhone 16 (test) | 21 | **19.53** | 0.21 mm |

So a 2 mm grain is 9 pixels in most training images but 39 pixels in an iPhone 16 test image. That's the real domain shift — much bigger than the lighting or colour. Fix: resample every image to a common px/mm (~4.58) before anything touches a model. Host confirms the camera was always **exactly 21 cm** from the soil, and I verified scale is fully determined by camera type with zero per-image variation — so this normalization is exact, not approximate.

**2. You are basically predicting one number, not eleven.**

I ran PCA on the 24 label curves. PC1 carries **91.4% of the variance and correlates 0.995 with log₁₀(D50)**. Reconstruction error by how many numbers you get right:

| numbers predicted | best achievable EMD |
|---|---|
| 1 (just D50) | 20.5 |
| 2 | 11.0 |
| 3 | 7.4 |
| 11 (free) | 0, but you'd need ~1000 samples |

The labels are lab curves interpolated linearly on a log axis, so they're smooth and low-dimensional by construction. Think of it this way: every curve is a slide down an S-shape, and 91% of "which slide" is just "how far along the slide is the midpoint." With 24 samples, regressing 2–3 shape parameters is a real problem; regressing 11 free values is not. This should drive your whole output head — and it gives monotonic, valid outputs for free.

**3. Grain counting is a dead end, and I proved it rather than assumed it.**

I built a classical granulometer (adaptive threshold → connected components → equivalent-area diameters converted to mm via PPM). It scored **EMD ≈ 198**, which is *twice as bad as ignoring the images entirely*. Reason is finding 1: 11 of your 24 samples have D50 below 0.11 mm, meaning their particles are 0.5 pixels. They're physically invisible. For those samples the only available signal is texture and appearance, never measurement.

## Baselines — the number to beat

Measured on the training set with my metric reimplementation:

| | EMD |
|---|---|
| official trivial baseline (9.09% per bin) | 100.3 |
| copy some other sample's curve | 104.2 |
| naive granulometry | ~198 |
| **train global median curve (ignores images)** | **82.6** |
| perfect | 0 |

**82.6 is the wall.** Anything above it means your vision pipeline contributes nothing.

## Leaderboard intelligence — do not chase the public LB

The host answered the awkward questions directly:

- **Public LB uses a fixed 3 of the 10 test soils.** Final = 0.30·public + 0.70·private. So public feedback is one coin flip away from noise.
- Top scores (0.00001, 0.36, 0.92) are **public-LB probing**, not a leak — host reviewed the private board and says those scores are realistic. He's considering releasing more data.
- **H374 was re-photographed** because AmbrosM caught it looking mislabeled ("Where are the cobbles?"). It's the only Edge 60 Fusion sample, only 3 images, and the reported worst CV score. Treat it as suspect.
- **H031 was deleted** (lab ran out of soil) — that's why you have 24, not 25.
- Someone asked 7 hours ago whether published geotechnical reports for the test site names count as allowed external data under rule 2.6. Unanswered. Your test IDs are real sites (Airbus BS6-3, Kleinkummerfeld, Audorfring, Münster 9–10 m depth). That's a legitimate-rules loophole but it defeats the benchmark, and with 70% weighted on a private split the host may swap the test set. I'd leave it alone.

## Bugs in your current folder

# What to do about PPM

**Use it to resample pixels. Never feed it to the model as a feature.**

Three separate decisions:

**1. Correct the numbers first.** The CSV's PPM is at *native* resolution; your delivered files are downscaled. The real per-pixel scales are 4.597 (Motorola), 4.553 (Samsung), 12.465 (H374), 13.942 (iPhone 14), 19.525 (iPhone 16). Anyone using 11.492 and 26.33 is off by 2.5×.

**2. Canonical target = 4.58 px/mm, and the reason matters.** You might think "keep the test images sharp at 14 px/mm, that's more information." It isn't usable information. A 4.6 px/mm training image contains *zero* information below ~0.9 mm — those pixels were never captured. If you train at a fine scale you ask the model to learn from upscaled mush, then hand it genuinely sharp test images, and every texture statistic shifts. **Match information content, not pixel count.** Downsample test to 4.58 with proper area-averaging (box/LANCZOS, never plain bilinear — that's what made my earlier gap look worse than it is).

**3. Don't feed PPM as an input.** PPM is camera identity in disguise, and camera is your dominant nuisance variable — it explains up to 71% of texture variance. A model given PPM will happily use it to sort images by phone and learn nothing about soil.

Then **jitter the scale during training** (±30% around 4.58 px/mm). That makes the model tolerant of residual scale and blur error, which means you stop depending on picking the one perfect canonical scale.

---

# The plan

### STEP 1 — Build a manifest, not a folder walk
One CSV: `image_path, sample_id, split, camera, native_w/h, delivered_w/h, ppm_delivered, fov_mm`. Camera from EXIF. This is the only place PPM gets resolved, so no downstream code ever guesses from a filename.

### STEP 2 — Canonical preprocessing
Per image: EXIF-orient → resample to 4.58 px/mm → gray-world white balance → mask the dark tray border → emit fixed 128×128 px tiles (= 28 mm × 28 mm physical). Tiles are the unit the network sees; the **soil sample stays the unit of supervision**. That mismatch is the whole trick — it turns 127 labelled images into thousands of gradient-carrying tiles while never pretending a tile has its own GSD.

### STEP 3 — Camera-invariant augmentation, sized from measurement
I measured the Samsung/Motorola gap on the same soil: texture energy +63% to +124%, saturation +74%. So set augmentation ranges to *bracket* that, not to taste: random contrast gain ~[0.6, 2.0], saturation [0, 1.8], sharpen/blur, JPEG quality, sensor noise, per-channel gain jitter, and grayscale with p=0.3. This is the single cheapest defence against the thing that broke my nearest-neighbour test.

### STEP 4 — Fix validation before touching a model
Leave-one-family-out over the 6 soil families the clustering found:
- **A** H181 H183 H366 H367 H368 H371 H372 H374 H615
- **B** H037 H038 H637  **C** H516  **D** F827 H126 H405 H549 H668
- **E** G190 H030 H493 H617 H666  **F** H616

Plain leave-one-sample-out will report a fantasy score because H366's twin H371 sits in the training fold. 6 folds also divides neatly onto 2 GPUs — run two folds at a time, three rounds.

### STEP 5 — Baseline ladder, and calibrate your scorer
Submit the global median curve **once**. Locally it scores 82.6; whatever Kaggle returns calibrates my EMD reimplementation against theirs and simultaneously tells you how the 3 public soils differ from the training mean. That's legitimate metric validation, not leaderboard probing. Your ladder: 100.3 trivial → 82.6 no-image → you must be clearly under 82.6 before any of this is working.

### STEP 6 — Frozen pretrained features first, no fine-tuning
**DINOv2 ViT-S/14, fully frozen**, patch tokens pooled per tile → per-image → per-sample, then a small MLP head. Reason: DINOv2 features are structure/texture oriented rather than semantic-class oriented, they're excellent at absurdly low label counts, and torch.hub serves them on Kaggle. Add my camera-corrected DoG vector (e1…e16, already 0.83 rank-correlation with log D50, zero training) as side inputs. Frozen + 5k head parameters is the highest-value-per-hour step in this whole plan and it may well be most of your score.

### STEP 7 — 4-parameter output head, not 11
PC1 alone is 91.4% of label variance and correlates 0.995 with log₁₀(D50). Reconstruction floors: rank-1 → 20.5, rank-2 → 11.0, rank-3 → 7.4. So predict **mean curve + 3 PC coefficients** = 4 numbers for 24 samples. Add monotone projection (clip to [0,100], cummax, force 200 mm = 100) — needed because raw rank-3 reconstructions break monotonicity on 9/24 samples. Loss = the metric itself, weighted-L1 on the log axis; it's differentiable as written.

### STEP 8 — Fine-tune gently, last block only
Unfreeze the final ~4 blocks at LR 1e-5 with the head at 1e-4, batch over tiles with per-sample gradient accumulation, early-stop on STEP 4 CV. With 24 labels, aggressive fine-tuning is how you go from 40 to 90, not the other way.

### STEP 9 — Attention pooling for the multi-image aggregation
Per-tile embeddings → learned attention → sample embedding. This is multiple-instance learning, and it's what lets 6–8 photos of one soil vote instead of being averaged. Also gives you a free interpretability check: attention weights should land on clast-rich regions for gravels.

### STEP 10 — Optional but strong: self-supervised pretraining on all 162 images
DINOv2 is frozen on natural images; a short masked-autoencoder / DINO pass over **train + test images, labels unused** adapts the backbone to soil texture *and* to the iPhone co

## 0. Corrections to your measured facts (verified this session)

All your numbers reproduce except three, and two of the three change the design:

| Your claim | Measured | Impact |

| tile counts 22999 / 8362 / 6427 / 3100 | FOV-preserving 4.58-px/mm canvas is **236.0 Mpx**, giving **12728 / 4128 / 2718 / 1164**. Your four numbers imply a canvas of 378–420 Mpx (their 224 and 256 values are consistent with each other at ~420 Mpx, so this is a canvas-area error, not overlap). ~420 Mpx ≈ tiling every image as a uniform ~1600×1600 array — i.e. a **uniform-pixel** canvas, which is exactly what §5 forbids. | Re-baseline disk/time budget. Recompute counts in the pipeline; do not carry them as constants. |
| — | **Not in your audit: 38 files carry a wide-gamut ICC profile; 124 carry none.** Test = Apple `mntr/RGB/acspAPPL` (35) reported as **Display P3**; H374 = `acspMTK` (3) also P3-family. The 124 EXIF-less training JPEGs are untagged → decoded as sRGB. | A genuine, unfitted, physically-grounded colour mismatch exists: **test pixels are P3, train pixels are sRGB**. §9 must handle it. |

All 162 files: baseline JPEG (SOF0), 8-bit, 3-component YCbCr, 4:2:0 subsampled (`34/17/17`), no progressive. So chroma is already half-res in *every* camera — do not spend design effort on chroma precision, and do not write canonical PNGs from a chroma-lossy source believing you recovered it.

Also confirmed: `ppm_updated.csv` Motorola row says `motorola edge 20`, not "Motorola Edge" — your `camera` key and the CSV's `phone` key are different strings; join on `phone`.

## 1. Decomposition

**Recommend a `preprocess/` package, not root scripts.** Four reasons: (a) the 13 stages below share one config object, one manifest schema, and one assertion set — as flat scripts that becomes 13 copies of `TARGET_PPM`; (b) this phase's whole value is *cross-checking*, which requires imported functions, not `exec`-style scripts; (c) `training_image_organization.py` / `test_image_organization.py` are the provenance of the current `Training/`/`Test/` layout — leave them untouched and unimported at root rather than folding them in and risking edits; (d) `python -m preprocess` gives resumable stages, which matters because a 236-Mpx resample pass takes minutes and you will re-run the audit more than the resample.

```
preprocess/__init__.py
preprocess/config.py        # single source of every constant; frozen dataclass + to_json() stamped into each audit artifact
preprocess/inventory.py     # enumerate, EXT-filter (excludes the 24 labels.csv), sha256 baseline, source-dir guard
preprocess/cameras.py       # filename->camera regex (tolerant), ppm_updated.csv join, EXIF/ICC probe, provenance arbitration
preprocess/geometry.py      # orientation canonicalisation, short/long pairing, effective PPM, agreement flags, FOV
preprocess/resample.py      # Pillow resample to canonical grid, no-upscale + FOV assertions
preprocess/soilmask.py      # illumination-normalised mask -> maximal inscribed crop rect + soil_fraction
preprocess/colour.py        # ICC->sRGB; gray-world GAINS computed+returned as params (application is opt-in)
preprocess/tiling.py        # grid math, manifest rows, opt-in materialisation of one size
preprocess/manifest.py      # schema (dtypes, enums, non-null), validators, CSV writers
preprocess/audit.py         # §16 report + every pass/fail assertion; non-zero exit on failure
preprocess/qc_sheets.py     # §17 contact sheets
preprocess/verify.py        # information-preservation measurements (§10 below)
preprocess/run.py           # CLI: --stage {inventory,geometry,resample,mask,tiles,audit,qc,verify} --all --dry-run
```

Outputs (your §6/§13/§16/§17):
```
data/training_down/<sample_id>/<stem>.png                 # canonical images only
data/testing_down/<ascii_slug>/<stem>.png
data/processed_meta/manifest_images.csv                   # §3 single source of truth
data/processed_meta/manifest_tiles.csv                    # §13
data/processed_meta/manifest_samples.csv                  # §12 hierarchy + labels
data/processed_meta/masks/<split>/<sample>/<stem>_mask.png
data/processed_meta/audit.{md,json}  camera_table.csv  flags.csv
data/processed_meta/golden_checks.json                    # §10 thresholds
data/qc/sheets/<split>/<sample>/<stem>.png                # §17
data/qc/paired_texture.csv  scale_ruler.csv
```
Keep the two image dirs pure (images only) so "no augmentation on disk" is visually auditable. Note `.gitignore` is `data/` — all output is untracked by design; `_look/` **is** tracked, so never write pipeline output there.

## 2. Manifest schema (`manifest_images.csv`)

One row per source image, 162 rows. Grouped by provenance:

**Identity / hierarchy** — `image_id` (sha256 of relative path, first 12 hex, stable PK), `source_path` (relpath, forward slashes), `processed_path`, `split` ∈{train,test}, `sample_id`, `site`, `soil_family`, `cv_group` (= `sample_id`), `filename`, `n_images_in_sample`.
- `site`: train → `NA`; test → leading token before borehole code (`Airbus`, `Kleinkummerfeld`, `Audorfring`, `Münster`, `Testfeld Lidl WHV`) → 5 sites / 10 samples.
- `soil_family`: train → letter-prefix + first digit (`F8`,`G1`,`H0`,`H1`,`H2`,`H3`,`H4`,`H5`,`H6`); test → `site`. Grouped CV can then split on either without re-deriving.
- Test dirs use `ascii_slug` (ü→ue, `,`→`_`, collapse non-alphanumerics) as the folder name; `sample_id` preserves the original. This is not cosmetic: `ü` round-tripped as mojibake in my own console output this session, and the mapping is 10/10 verified agai

- `soil_family`: train → letter-prefix + first digit (`F8`,`G1`,`H0`,`H1`,`H2`,`H3`,`H4`,`H5`,`H6`); test → `site`. Grouped CV can then split on either without re-deriving.

# Soil-GSD Preprocessing Pipeline — Implementation Plan

## Context

**Why:** the Kaggle competition *Predicting Soil Grain Size Distributions from Images* (id 139732)
asks for 11 cumulative grain-size fractions per soil sample from photographs. There are only 24
labelled soil samples behind 127 images. Before any model work, the image data needs a
deterministic, audited preprocessing layer that puts every photograph on a common *physical*
scale and records provenance, because three properties of this dataset silently break naive
pipelines:

1. The competition's `ppm_updated.csv` quotes PPM at **native camera resolution**, but the
   delivered training JPEGs were downscaled before release. Using those numbers is a 2.5× error.
2. Camera pipeline explains up to **71% of texture-feature variance** — more than which soil is in
   the frame — so scale and provenance must be recorded, not guessed.
3. EXIF exists on only **38 of 162** images, so the obvious "read metadata from EXIF" plan is
   unsatisfiable for 77% of the corpus.

**Outcome of this phase:** a manifest-driven, reproducible preprocessing pipeline that emits
physically-normalised images plus tile metadata plus a loud audit. **No models, no training, no
feature learning, no prediction heads, no Kaggle score work.**

**Decisions already taken** (each confirmed against measurement, see *Findings that change the
spec*):

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Canonical scale | **Derived, not typed**: `TARGET_PPM = min(effective_ppm over all cameras) = 4.5526 px/mm` |
| Photometrics on disk | Bake geometry + **Display P3 → sRGB**; store gray-world gains as **parameters** |
| Tiles | Manifest coordinates for all four sizes; **materialise 256 px only** |
| Masking | Per-image **inscribed crop rectangle**, capped 15%/axis; never per-pixel deletion |

## Findings that change the spec — read before implementing

These are measured, not assumed. Three contradict the brief.

**(1) `4.58 px/mm` and "never upscale" are mutually exclusive.** Samsung A52 effective PPM is
4.5539 (geometric mean) / 4.5526 (long axis) — *below* 4.58. Reaching 4.58 forces a 0.57% upscale
on all 55 Samsung images. Resolved by deriving the target as the minimum over cameras: every one
of the 162 images then becomes identity-or-downsample, and residual cross-camera scale error is
**0.07%**, which is what lets later phases attribute any remaining difference to camera pipeline
rather than geometry.

**(2) "Camera from EXIF, filename as fallback" is impossible.** EXIF is present on 38/162 (all 35
test + all 3 H374). The 69 Motorola Edge and 55 Samsung A52 training images have **no EXIF block
at all**. Inverted: filename is the primary camera key (measured 100% parse rate, zero unknowns),
and EXIF acts only as a *validator that can raise a flag, never as a source*. A `camera_source`
column records which path produced each value.

**(3) A verified colour-space mismatch nobody had recorded.** 38 files carry an embedded ICC
profile; 124 carry none. The H374 profile's own description string reads `Display P3`, and its red
primary decodes to chromaticity **(0.682, 0.319)** — Display P3's (0.680, 0.320), not sRGB's
(0.640, 0.330). The iPhone files carry byte-identical primaries. So **all 35 test images and all 3
H374 images are Display P3; the remaining 124 training images decode as sRGB.** P3→sRGB conversion
is a correctness fix using zero fitted parameters, so it is baked.

| Edge 60 Fusion | 0.37 | 0.44 | 0.39 | 0.35 (no rim) |
| Samsung A52 | **0.82** | 0.64 | 0.47 | 0.32 (strong rim) |
| iPhone 14 / 16 | 0.68 / **0.79** | 0.57 / 0.55 | 0.44 / 0.41 | 0.33 / 0.32 (strong rim) |
